description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Sir Peter Westmacott, former UK Ambassador to the US, says King Charles III's speech to Congress focused on the "importance of the relationship" between the US and UK while stressing NATO solidarity. Michelle Brouhard, Head of Policy and Geopolitical Risk at Kpler, says the UAE's exit reflects a long-running rift within OPEC, calling it a "new chapter." Representative Sean Casten (D-IL) criticizes Energy Secretary Chris Wright’s comments that demand for US energy exports is growing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: King Charles Addresses Congress in US Visit | Balance of Power: Late Edition 04/28/2026

author: Courtney McBride, Erik Wasson
description: Key congressional Republicans are poised to break with Donald Trump on his proposed 44% raise for the Pentagon, a rare act of defiance that signals the president’s weakening grip on Washington as the midterm elections near and he quickly approaches the back half of his second term.
title: Trump’s $1.5 Trillion Defense Plan Draws Rare Republican Pushback

description: King Charles III called on the US to maintain its leadership role in the world in a remarkably pointed speech for a monarch that urged Americans to resist the pull of isolationism. Ellen Milligan has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: King Charles Urges US to Reject Isolationism in Landmark Speech

description: Michelle Brouhard, Head of Policy and Geopolitical Risk at Kpler, says the UAE's exit reflects a long-running rift within OPEC, calling it a "new chapter" after years with "one foot in and one foot out." She pushes back on claims Iran is collapsing, saying it has faced pressure "for about five or six years," but warns the country may have only "five or six days" before shutting oil wells due to storage constraints. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran May Shut Oil Wells in 5-6 Days: Kpler's Brouhard

description: Sir Peter Westmacott, former UK Ambassador to the US, says King Charles III's speech to Congress focused on the "importance of the relationship" between the US and UK while stressing NATO solidarity. Sir Westmacott highlights the King's concern over Ukraine and his warning against isolationism, and says President Donald Trump has "always had a soft spot for the British monarchy" and views the King as a "close friend," despite more "frayed" ties with Prime Minister Keir Starmer. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fmr. Ambassador on King Charles III's Address to Congress

author: Joe Mayes
description: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves has won a battle for the authority to force pension funds to invest a proportion of their assets in the country, one of her economic growth initiatives that had been stymied by the House of Lords.
title: Reeves Wins Battle for Power to Require Pensions to Invest in UK

description: Democratic Congressman Sean Casten of Illinois, who was in the chamber for King Charles III's speech, says the remarks highlighted the transatlantic relationship between the US-UK, the importance of supporting Ukraine and the rule of law in a "subtle" but clear way. Reacting to Energy Secretary Chris Wright’s comments that demand for US energy exports is growing, Rep. Casten criticizes an “extractive” approach and says policy uncertainty is “greatly” confusing investors. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Casten on King's Address, Energy Investment

As well as how Transatlantic alliance more important now than ever pointing out that the US, and allies are the heart of NATO and that the  US-UK defense ties are measured in not 'years but decades'. 

King Charles also condemned shooting attempt at WH Correspondents Dinner.  (Source: Bloomberg)

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power,  Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss King Charles' visit to Washington and his attempt to heal bonds torn by tariffs and the war in Iran. On today's show, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Partner at Stonecourt Capital Rick Davis, and Province of Ontario Minister of Finance Peter Bethlenfalvy. In addition, Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow interviews AWS CEO Mark Garman. (Source: Bloomberg)

description:
The United Arab Emirates will leave OPEC next month, in a significant blow to the group that raises questions about its future at a time when the industry is grappling with the massive supply disruption caused by the Iran war. 
The UAE’s exit May 1 after six decades of membership is the culmination of years of tension with OPEC leader Saudi Arabia both over oil output policy and competition for regional political influence. It’s also the latest indication of how the conflict is reshaping global energy markets: While the UAE has talked in the past about quitting OPEC, Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei said in an interview that the disruption caused by the war created an opportune time for the move. Mia Gindis, Bloomberg News Oil Markets Reporter joins to discuss on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UAE Quits OPEC as War Upends Oil Markets and Gulf Tensions Rise

author: Katrina Manson
description: Google has reached an agreement with the US Defense Department to allow its artificial intelligence systems to be used for classified military work, according to a Pentagon official, a deal that came together as researchers at the company protested against it.
title: Google Allows Pentagon to Use Its AI in Classified Military Work
